Subject: SLA scenarios & benchmark plan for reserved throughput — next steps

Alex — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we schedule the pilot run: 

Call highlights
- Workload: streaming text generation (server-side streaming of token chunks) for clinical summarization. Typical response ~350 tokens (mean), occasionally up to 1200 tokens for long notes.
- Concurrency: ~150 long-lived streaming connections during peak, expected burst concurrency up to 400 for short windows.
- Target SLOs: P50 first-byte streaming latency < 200 ms, P95 first-byte < 900 ms; end-to-end (full response) P95 < 2.5s for median-length responses.
- Throughput: baseline steady-state 40 requests/sec (350 tokens), peak sustained burst 120 reqs/sec for 3–5 minutes.
- Other constraints: encrypted KV cache mandatory, no customer data leaves NovaMed region, and SOC2 evidence may be requested during procurement.

Attached is a filled worksheet (sla-scenarios-specs.xlsx) with the example payloads and tokenization stats you gave us. Can you confirm the typical prompt+response token split we should use for benchmarks (I used 90/260 in the sheet) and whether you want us to prioritize H100 or try an H100 vs A100 vs L4 comparison?

Proposed next steps
1) You share a small set of representative prompts and one long-note example (if possible) — we can use these for token-profile accuracy.
2) Redwood runs three scenarios in our dedicated pilot: steady-state (40 RPS), burst (120 RPS for 5m), and concurrency streaming test (150 persistent streams + 400-peak).
3) We’ll test three GPU profiles: H100 (float/AMP), A100 (int8 quantized where available), and L4 (aggressive quantized profile) and report cost/latency tradeoffs.
4) Book a 4-hour pilot window next week — we’ll need Maya/Procurement in the loop for any contractual/region controls.

If that plan looks good I’ll assign Karthik for the bench design and Ben for ops runbook.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Laura — thanks for the recap and for filling out the sheet. Confirming a few things and adding context from our side: 

- Token split: 80 prompt / 270 response is more typical for our production traffic (we see slightly longer responses on average). Please use 80/270 as the default, but include your 90/260 runs as a sensitivity case.
- Streaming behavior: we stream tokens as soon as they are generated; first-byte latency is critical for UX so please include both first-byte and first-chunk metrics.
- KV cache: must be encrypted at rest; we can share a sample cache key set if needed.
- Region/compliance: we need all pilot infra to be in us-east-1. SOC2 evidence request will come from our security team during the procurement window.

We would like Redwood to include both H100 and L4 (quantized) in the initial matrix. If H100 shows a clear win for the first-byte SLO at target concurrency, we’ll consider adding A100 for a middle-ground cost point but it’s lower priority.

I’ve attached the run commands we use for our internal bench harness (runbook-benchmark-commands.txt) — feel free to use or adapt. Also CC’ing Maya (product lead) and procurement to get the calendar and NDAs in place.

On Fri, Sep 7, 2028 at 5:30 PM, Alex Reed <alex@streamly.ai> wrote:
> Laura — thanks for the recap and for filling out the sheet. Confirming a few things and adding context from our side: 
> 
> - Token split: 80 prompt / 270 response is more typical...

Thanks — I put together a concrete bench matrix below based on the token split and streaming requirements you both confirmed. This is what we’ll run in the pilot and how we’ll map results to Dedicated capacity sizing and a recommended reserved throughput.

Planned benchmark scenarios (each run will include 3 repeats):
1) Steady-state baseline
   - Payload: 80/270 tokens, concurrency: 40 RPS sustained, duration: 30m
   - Metrics: first-byte P50/P95, first-chunk P50/P95, per-token cost, GPU utilization, KV cache hit ratio
2) Burst stress
   - Payload: 80/270, load: 120 RPS sustained for 5m, preceded/followed by 10m ramp up/down
   - Metrics: tail latency (P95/P99), CPU/GPU memory pressure, queue depth, fallback rate if any
3) Streaming concurrency test (priority)
   - 150 long-lived streams (idle heartbeats), concurrently creating new streams to simulate spikes to 400 active streams
   - Measure: first-byte for initial chunk, inter-chunk gaps, p99 end-to-end for medium (350 token) responses
4) Long-response edge case
   - Single request 1200-token response under synthetic mid-load to capture KV cache and kv-cache-resume behavior

GPU profiles to evaluate (cost vs SLO tradeoff):
- H100 (fp16 / amp): expected best latency at high concurrency, higher cost — target for meeting first-byte P95 < 900ms under 150 concurrent streams.
- A100 (int8 / clipped quant): mid-cost option; sometimes close to H100 for shorter sequences but can show higher variance on streaming.
- L4 (aggressive quantized profile): low-cost; expect higher first-byte and inter-chunk delays but may be acceptable for non-real-time paths.

Acceptance gating (how we decide capacity recommendation):
- If H100 meets first-byte P95 < 900ms and P99 < 1.5s at 150 streams, recommend Reserved H100 slab sized for 40 steady-state RPS with headroom for 2.5x bursts (i.e., plan for 100 RPS sustained headroom).
- If A100 matches within 15% of H100 latency at target SLOs, propose A100 as a cost compromise with a 25% larger reserved slab to maintain SLOs under burst.
- If only L4 meets cost targets but fails first-byte targets, recommend hybrid routing: critical traffic -> H100, background batch traffic -> L4.

Operational notes:
- We’ll enable prefix KV caching and pin hot-key cache to avoid repeated tensor-decoding for templated prompts.
- Batching: we’ll test with continuous batching (max batch latency 5ms) and per-request low-latency mode.

Requested from Streamly:
- Provide representative prompt set (4 short, 2 medium, 1 long) by Mon 9/10 EOD.
- Confirm us-east-1 constraint and any encryption/KMS endpoints (for KV cache).
- Confirm a 4-hour pilot window on Wed 9/13 or Thu 9/14.

I’ll push the bench scripts into the CI link Laura shared and capture results in the Drive doc for easy review.

Karthik Iyer
